correctness.rationale: Connected weighted Laplacians give J=sum_{u<v}R_uv=tr(W L^-1), strictly convex in distinct positive edge conductances; connected boundary divergence and budget scaling produce a unique minimizer. For t=0, series path J=sum Aℓ/cℓ, optimal cℓ^0=B sqrt(Aℓ)/H, Lagrange multiplier H²/B². A unit chord current produces potential z_k clamped between cumulative resistances h_i,h_j. Differentiating total resistance under adding the chord gives -lambda times pairwise potential dispersion Q=n∑(z_k−mean)^2. KKT and strict convexity establish zero-chord optimum iff q>=Q, including boundary equality, while direct t>0 perturbation improves q<Q. Nondecreasing clipped profiles and positive covariance prove strict nesting of chord intervals. Riemann sums of h→2 arcsin sqrt(s) yield explicit clipped-arcsine variance. An exact double sum Q=n−1+2Σ_j b(j/n)Σ_{i<j}a(i/n) combined with square-root power sums and weighted trapezoid errors gives endpoint (π²/4−2)n²+2πζ(−1/2)√n+O(log n). Independent finite-difference and variance checks support the analytic steps; independently calculated endpoint residuals after two leading terms for n=100,400,1600,6400,16000 stay small and log-like, but are not an asymptotic proof.
residual_risks: The O(log n) error depends on uniform endpoint power-sum/trapezoidal estimates, not established by numerical residuals; source provides a weighted error bound requiring legitimate singular-endpoint handling.
